lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The older Student Investment Fund entry should be shortened or removed.
items.because: It gives space to an older, duplicated claim instead of more relevant experience.

items.says: Education appears before experience despite several years of post-degree work.
items.because: Placing education first delays the more relevant work history.

items.says: The experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Crescent Bank appears above the more recent Stonebridge Manufacturing role, making the section harder to scan chronologically.

items.says: The caddie duties are given without an outcome for members.
The current caddie role is described in past tense.
The tournament bullet does not say what work you personally handle.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what skills or responsibilities “helped the pro shop run” demonstrates.

items.says: The tournament work is described in past tense despite being part of a current role.
items.because: “Helped” can make the status of the responsibility unclear.

items.says: The tournament bullet gives no result or measure of the contribution.
The declined-application result should appear before the loan-underwriting bullet.
The declined-application analysis is not identified.
“My findings” uses a first-person pronoun.
“Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in December 2022.
items.because: It makes checklist writing sound like a current Crescent Bank responsibility, with no indication the work continued.

items.says: The 40% close-efficiency figure has no defined measure or comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what “efficiency” means or interpret the change without a baseline.

items.says: The shared template’s standardization is described without its effect.
The explanation of the shared template is longer than needed.
The board-pack commentary is named without saying what it changed or informed.
The useful scope detail comes after the main action and is wordy.
The valuation method pairs free cash flow to equity with the wrong discount rate.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity should be discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is generally used for free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The acquisition valuation has no result or stated use.
items.because: A reader cannot assess what it produced or how it related to the acquisition decision.

items.says: The method comes before the valuation result, if one is available.
Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: A group margin uses total group EBITDA divided by total group revenue, or a revenue-weighted average of unit margins.

items.says: The 45% group margin has no comparison point.
The stated method follows the 45% claim and can make it read as a consolidated margin.
The forecast and debt-repayment achievement is also attributed to the Student Investment Fund entry.
items.because: The same forecast period, business size, error rate and debt repayment appear in both roles, leaving unclear which role owns the outcome.

items.says: “Monthly forecast error under 4%” does not define how the error was measured.
items.because: Without the measure or calculation, a reader cannot interpret or compare the accuracy figure.

items.says: The forecast results should lead the bullet rather than follow its method and company-size context.
The strong forecast result should open the Stonebridge entry.
The 6% comparison does not identify the market-price benchmark.
items.because: A reader cannot tell when the valuation was compared with the market.

items.says: The discount-rate change does not specify its direction or rate context.
items.because: A reader cannot tell the starting rate, which scenario produced each value, or whether “1-point” means a percentage point.

items.says: “It” has an unclear referent after two deliverables are named.
The generic FP&A description does not name a specific action or what the work produced.
items.because: “Supported” and “financial reporting and analysis” do not show a concrete personal contribution or result.

items.says: The report is described without the result of its benchmark comparison.
The committee-use clause is long and follows the report’s main result.
The benchmark-report contribution should come before the other student-fund bullets.
The cash-forecast achievement is also attributed to the Stonebridge role.
items.because: The matching forecast period, business size, error rate and debt repayment read as the same accomplishment in two entries.

items.says: The forecast bullet does not say what drove or informed the forecast.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the work involved beyond producing the forecast.

items.says: The forecast error figure does not identify how the error was measured.
items.because: Without a calculation method, a reader cannot interpret or compare the accuracy figure.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund entry does not form a focused student-fund story.
items.because: The generic FP&A line and cash-forecast achievement pull it away from its relevant benchmark-report contribution.
